preamble: In the Galician gheada the voiced velar stop /ɡ/ is replaced by a back fricative, and one of its realizations is the voiced uvular fricative [ʁ]. In an acoustic survey of gheada speakers, voiced uvular fricatives made up 11.5% of tokens, alongside commoner pharyngeal, glottal and velar outcomes; voiced variants occur mainly between vowels in inland villages. The change is confined to western Galician.

examples.note: Inland villages favour uvular, pharyngeal or glottal fricatives, which are often voiced between vowels; Wikipedia transcribes the commonest variant as pharyngeal, pago [ˈpaħʊ].

examples.from: /ɡ/ of the test words in Labraña-Barrero & van Oosterzee (2003)
examples.to: voiced uvular fricative [ʁ] in 11.5% of tokens
examples.note: The same survey found unvoiced uvular [χ] in 8.3% of tokens and uvular approximants as a further variant.

sources: Labraña-Barrero, S., & van Oosterzee, C. (2003). An Acoustic Approach to Galician Gheada. Proceedings of the 15th International Congress of Phonetic Sciences, Barcelona, 945–948. https://www.internationalphoneticassociation.org/icphs-proceedings/ICPhS2003/papers/p15_0945.pdf
